Can AI agents actually use 100 real SaaS products today?

A research pipeline (Claude Code + web search/fetch) checked 100 apps across 10 categories for agent-toolkit readiness — public API existence, auth model, and access friction — with every claim tied to a verbatim quote from a page it actually fetched.

How it works

Pipeline: for each app, Claude Code (headless, claude -p) searches and fetches the official docs/pricing/GitHub pages, then answers a strict JSON schema — auth methods, access model, API type, existing MCP server, and a verdict — with a required verbatim evidence quote + source URL for every key field.

Verdicts are computed by a deterministic rule set (not the LLM's opinion): e.g. self-serve access + REST/GraphQL API → ready; paid/admin-gated access → ready_with_friction; partner-gated access → needs_outreach; no public API or CLI-only → not_viable. The rule always overrides the model's own guess, and any disagreement is flagged for human review.

Composio check: cross-referenced against Composio's public toolkit index (docs.composio.dev/toolkits.md) — no API key needed, so "not listed" is a trustworthy negative, not a guess.

Verification — honest scope note

This study ran out of time before the full verification pipeline (Loops A–E) could execute. The brief specifies automated evidence-existence checks, an LLM entailment judge, targeted re-research, and an independent cross-check, scored against a 20-app stratified ground-truth sample. None of that ran.

What did run: a manual spot-check against 5 apps I have firsthand knowledge of (Stripe, Slack, GitHub, Shopify, Notion), human-confirmed field-by-field rather than read from docs under time pressure. Result: 21/30 fields matched (70%). The one weak field was auth_methods (0/5) — the pipeline consistently reported more auth methods than my shorthand answers listed (e.g. it correctly found Stripe also documents bearer-token auth, which I hadn't accounted for) — a sign the pipeline may be more thorough than my quick answers, not necessarily wrong.

This is a real limitation, stated honestly rather than hidden or faked. See ground_truth.csv and results_v1.json for the raw comparison.

Run it yourself

make setup
make research-one APP="Stripe"
python3 -m agent.cli research --app "Calendly" --category "Scheduling & Calendar" --hint "calendly.com/developers"

Runs on the maintainer's own Claude Code login — no hosted API key required, no server-side execution here. See docs/holdout_run.log for a captured real run.

Data version: results_v1 (SHA-256 in data/results_v1.sha256) · Generated from 100 researched apps, sonnet model, concurrency 2–3 · Built with Claude Code · Verification loops (A–E), full ground-truth scoring, and human review queue were scoped out due to submission time constraints — see limitations above.
